text:
Connor O'Brien: heads up for the release train: do we want the Private upgrade+rollback work to ship as part of a named Private release (e.g. Private 1.14) or as an "out-of-band" installer/chart update? Trying to lock scope for the next cut.

Sahana Iyer: +1 on deciding asap. If it’s in the named release we need to line up versions across:
- installer
- helm charts
- control plane (version endpoint + audit logs)
- observability pack dashboards
Otherwise we’re going to be chasing compatibility exceptions in RC.

Vivek Kulkarni: product POV: for customers this is definitely a “release feature” (they’ll ask “which version includes rollback”). I’d prefer it in a named Private release with explicit gates + docs.

Sean Gallagher: SRE POV: if it’s in the train, it can’t ship without the runbook + dashboards. Otherwise on-call gets paged with no visibility. :grimacing:

Connor O'Brien: ok, leaning toward “Private 1.14 includes upgrade/rollback v1” then. Question is: what are the hard gates vs “recommended”?

Neha Kapoor: hard gates from infra:
1) artifact signing + verification enforced for offline bundles (on-prem)
2) backup step has to have a verification pass (not just “snapshot created”)
3) rollback has guardrails for forward-only migrations (no "just do it")

Marcus Lin: +1. Security gate: installer must refuse unsigned bundle + emit audit event for upgrade/rollback actions. Also want evidence that signing keys aren’t baked into the bundle tooling.

Ethan Park: control plane pieces are in flight:
- version reporting endpoint used by installer prechecks
- migration metadata table to mark forward-only
- audit log event types (upgrade_start, upgrade_complete, rollback_start, rollback_blocked, etc)
We can have all of that in the release branch if we cut end of week.

Leila Farouk: release gate from testing side: at least one automated “fail mid-upgrade then rollback” integration test in CI has to be green on the release tag. I’m ok with limited matrix at GA, but not zero.

Allison Grant: observability gate: upgrade controller/installer structured logs + correlation id in control plane logs. If we ship without correlation id it’s a needle-in-haystack situation.

Connor O'Brien: for reference, current PR/status list:
- installer: `upgrade plan` + compat validation (PR #418)
- precheck runner (PR #421)
- backup snapshot+verify (PR #427)
- rollback command (PR #433)
- offline bundle import + signature verification (PR #439)
- structured logs + diagnostics tarball (PR #444)
- integration test harness (PR #452)
- charts: migration gating + hooks (charts PR #205), rollback hooks/annotations (charts PR #224)
- control plane: version endpoint (redwood PR #18431), audit logs (PR #18477), migration metadata (PR #18510), correlation id propagation (PR #18544)

release-bot: Reminder: Private 1.14 branch cut proposed for Thu 18:00 PT. RC0 build starts automatically after cut.

Rafael Mendes: runbook is in draft but needs final "what to monitor" section once dashboards are finalized. Also need the rollback decision tree (when rollback is blocked due to migrations) spelled out.

Kira Thompson: docs gate from me: customer-facing page needs:
- prerequisites (k8s version, storage class, snapshot permissions)
- expected downtime window guidance
- how to generate diagnostics bundle + what Support will ask for
If this is in a named release, it needs to be in the release notes too.

Markus Klein: beta pilots angle: if we ship in the named release, I want it behind a feature flag default-off for GA week, default-on after 1-2 successful customer upgrades. That gives PS some safety net.

Vivek Kulkarni: I’m ok with “feature available” in 1.14 but “enabled by default” later, as long as docs explain it. We should avoid customers thinking rollback is magical if migrations block it.

Sean Gallagher: +1. Also: for release gate we need alert thresholds for upgrade failures so we can see if 1.14 is spiking. Otherwise we won’t notice until a customer escalates.

Sahana Iyer: proposing explicit gates for inclusion in Private 1.14:
G0 (must-have to cut branch):
- compat matrix enforced (installer fails fast with actionable error)
- signed artifacts + verification (offline + online)
- prechecks JSON output (support ingestion)

G1 (must-have for RC1):
- backup snapshot+verify wired into upgrade flow
- rollback command works for “no forward-only migrations” case
- audit log events emitted

G2 (must-have for GA tag):
- integration test for rollback in CI
- dashboards (upgrade step duration/failures) + runbook finalized
- docs + release notes merged

Connor O'Brien: this looks right. only question: do we treat correlation id as G1 or G2?

Allison Grant: correlation id should be G1. Without it, the diagnostics tarball loses a lot of value (can’t stitch installer step -> service logs). It’s a small code change but huge for triage.

Marcus Lin: agreeing with Allison. Also correlation id in audit logs would be nice-to-have but at minimum logs.

Ethan Park: can land correlation id propagation this week. We already have a header/field in the control plane request context; just need to thread it through the upgrade endpoints.

Connor O'Brien: cool. action items:
- @Sahana Iyer formalize gates in the GA checklist doc and pin in channel
- @Rafael Mendes + @Sean Gallagher finalize runbook + alert thresholds by RC1
- @Kira Thompson draft release notes + docs stub for “feature flag default off” language
- I’ll update release train doc: Private 1.14 includes upgrade/rollback v1 subject to G0/G1/G2

Vivek Kulkarni: :thumbsup: please also note in release notes the limitations: no guaranteed zero downtime, rollback may be blocked by forward-only migrations, and on-prem requires signed offline bundles.

Connor O'Brien: will do. I’ll post an update after tomorrow’s sync once we confirm PR landing dates.
